 New York enters the matchup looking to snap a two-game losing streak after falling 106-104 to the Indiana Pacers on Friday. Jalen Brunson continues to lead the Knicks offensively, averaging 26.6 points per game, while Karl-Anthony Towns provides a dominant presence in the paint. The defending NBA champions have struggled with consistency early in the season, but a victory over Toronto would help them regain momentum as they look to climb the Eastern Conference standings.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Toronto is also looking to get back on track after dropping three consecutive games, including a 123-112 loss to Philadelphia on Thursday. RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley have been key contributors for the Raptors, while Scottie Barnes remains questionable with a groin injury and Kawhi Leonard is sidelined with a knee issue. Sunday's matchup also features an intriguing reunion, with Barrett and Quickley facing their former team and OG Anunoby returning to Toronto, where he spent the early years of his NBA career.
